answer: Each agent stakes a token‑backed reputation on a public terrace of signed attestations; the cost to acquire a new identity is a saffron‑priced proof‑of‑work that also emits a zephyr of random challenges. The ledger applies quadratic weighting, so the influence of n new identities grows as √n while a single long‑standing node retains linear weight. An attacker must therefore expend the square of the desired influence, making mass Sybil creation prohibitively expensive.
